Empirical Research Plan  
“Does inclusion in Fortune’s ‘100 Best Companies to Work For’ predict future stock returns?”

----------------------------------------------------
1. Identification Strategy
----------------------------------------------------
Choice:  Difference-in-Differences (DiD) with staggered treatment adoption, combined with firm-level risk-adjusted return estimation (Fama-French-Carhart factor model).

Why it fits:
•  The Fortune list is a discrete, dated, public event.  
•  Some firms appear in some years and not others, creating natural on/off variation (“staggered shocks”).  
•  DiD compares the change in risk-adjusted returns for firms that enter (or re-enter) the list to the contemporaneous change for observationally similar firms that are not yet (or never) listed.  
•  By residualising returns on the 4-factor model before the DiD, we net out standard priced risk, so any remaining difference can be interpreted as abnormal performance attributable to the information in employee satisfaction.

Econometric form (Sun-Abraham staggered-DiD to avoid two-way‐FE bias):

AR_it  =  Σ_k≠-1 β_k·D_i,t+k  +  γ_i  +  λ_t  +  ε_it

AR_it         = monthly abnormal return of firm i in month t  
D_i,t+k       = leads (k<0) and lags (k≥0) of first-time-listing indicator  
γ_i, λ_t      = firm and calendar-month fixed effects  
β_k (k≥0)     = causal effect of inclusion k months after first appearance  
Test of interest:  β_0 … β_24  > 0 ?  (24-month window)

----------------------------------------------------
2. Treatment and Control
----------------------------------------------------
Treatment variable  
•  Treat_i,t  = 1 for firm i starting the month after its FIRST appearance on the list and staying 1 for the next 24 months (baseline horizon).  
•  Separate indicator for RE-entries can be added as robustness but baseline focuses on the information in first-time inclusion.

Control group  
•  (a) “Never-treated” firms in the same Fama-French 49 industry that are matched on size decile, book-to-market quintile and past 12-month momentum decile.  
•  (b) “Not-yet-treated” firms that will enter in the future but have not yet been listed (absorbing THEMSELVES as controls before treatment).

Key variation  
•  Cross-section: treated vs matched control.  
•  Time: before vs after first listing date.

----------------------------------------------------
3. Key Identifying Assumptions
----------------------------------------------------
A1. Parallel trends  
Absent inclusion, treated firms’ risk-adjusted returns would have evolved in parallel to control firms.  
Plausibility: Matching on industry/size/BM/momentum plus firm & time FE helps; we will test visually with event-study leads (β_k for k<0 should ≈ 0).

A2. No anticipation  
The list is released mid-January; we assume investors cannot perfectly anticipate which firms will make it. We start treatment AFTER publication and check for pre-release price drift (again via leads).

A3. Stable Unit Treatment Value (no spillovers)  
One firm’s inclusion should not mechanically alter another’s returns (reasonable given diversified investor base; we will test by excluding same-industry peers as robustness).

A4. No simultaneous confounding shocks correlated with inclusion  
Fortune’s methodology is survey-based and not triggered by contemporaneous performance; we will partial-out earnings announcement windows (±3 days) in month 0 to reduce overlap.

----------------------------------------------------
4. Main Threats and Mitigations
----------------------------------------------------
T1. Selection on unobservables  
Firms that become “great workplaces” may concurrently improve other intangibles (brand, innovation) that investors also under-value.  
Fix: Control semi-parametrically for changes in intangibles proxies (R&D/Sales, advertisement expense, patent filings) where available; include firm FE to absorb time-invariant heterogeneity.

T2. Look-ahead / publication-date mis-timing  
If we line up returns incorrectly (e.g., using calendar year instead of exact announcement date) we could pick up pre-treatment returns.  
Fix: Use exact Fortune issue date (usually second Thursday of January) and drop the publication month \(t=0\) or use daily data to verify.

T3. Multiple appearances & treatment reversal  
Firms may enter, exit, and re-enter.  
Fix: Focus on first inclusion; treat later lists as separate, censor subsequent windows, and run robustness with dynamic treatment handling (Gardner 2022 approach).

----------------------------------------------------
5. R Code Outline (executable)
----------------------------------------------------
```r
# --------------------------------------------------
# 0. Packages
# --------------------------------------------------
library(data.table)     # fast data handling
library(lubridate)
library(broom)
library(fixest)         # Sun & Abraham DiD implemented
library(ggplot2)

# --------------------------------------------------
# 1. Load Data
# --------------------------------------------------
list   <- fread("fortune_best_companies_1984_2009.csv")   # cols: permno, list_year, pub_date
crsp_m <- fread("crsp_monthly_returns.csv")               # cols: permno, date, ret
factors<- fread("ff_carhart_factors.csv")                 # mkt_rf, smb, hml, mom, rf
chars  <- fread("compustat_chars.csv")                    # yearly size, bm, etc.

# --------------------------------------------------
# 2. Prep Variables
# --------------------------------------------------
# Monthly abnormal return (excess over 4-factor predicted)
crsp_m <- merge(crsp_m, factors, by = "date", all.x = TRUE)

crsp_m[, exret := ret - rf]

# estimate rolling betas (3y window) and compute abnormal return
setkey(crsp_m, permno, date)
crsp_m[, `:=`(mkt_ex = mkt_rf, smb_ex = smb, hml_ex = hml, mom_ex = mom)]

# fit betas firm-by-firm
betaFun <- function(dt){
    fit <- lm(exret ~ mkt_ex + smb_ex + hml_ex + mom_ex, data = dt)
    coef(fit)
}

betas <- crsp_m[, if (.N >= 36) betaFun(.SD), by = permno]   # simple illustration
setnames(betas, c("permno","alpha","beta_mkt","beta_smb","beta_hml","beta_mom"))
crsp_m <- merge(crsp_m, betas, by = "permno", all.x = TRUE)

crsp_m[, AR := exret - (beta_mkt*mkt_ex + beta_smb*smb_ex +
                         beta_hml*hml_ex + beta_mom*mom_ex)]

# --------------------------------------------------
# 3. Treatment Timing
# --------------------------------------------------
list[, first_pub := min(pub_date), by = permno]
treat_dates <- list[, .(permno, first_pub)]

crsp_m <- merge(crsp_m, treat_dates, by = "permno", all.x = TRUE)
crsp_m[, months_since := interval(first_pub %m+% months(1), date) %/% months(1)]
crsp_m[, treat := fifelse(months_since >= 0 & months_since <= 24, 1, 0)]
crsp_m[, rel_month := months_since]  # for event-study
crsp_m[months_since < -24 | months_since > 24, rel_month := NA] # limit window

# --------------------------------------------------
# 4. Matched Control Sample
# --------------------------------------------------
# Build year-level firm characteristics
chars[, fiscal_year := ymd(paste0(fyear,"-12-31"))]
chars_small <- chars[, .(permno, fiscal_year, size = log(mve),
                         bm = log(bm), mom12 = mom12)]

# merge and carry forward to months
crsp_m <- merge(crsp_m, chars_small, by = "permno", all.x = TRUE)
setorder(crsp_m, permno, date)
crsp_m[, size := nafill(size, type="locf"), by = permno]
crsp_m[, bm   := nafill(bm,   type="locf"), by = permno]
crsp_m[, mom12:= nafill(mom12,type="locf"), by = permno]

# Propensity score within industry-year
crsp_m[, ind := substr(sic,1,2)]   # placeholder for industry code
ps_model <- glm(treat ~ size + bm + mom12,
                data = crsp_m[year(date)==year(first_pub)], family=binomial)
crsp_m[, ps := predict(ps_model, type="response")]

# --------------------------------------------------
# 5. Main DiD Specification (Sun & Abraham)
# --------------------------------------------------
event_data <- crsp_m[!is.na(rel_month) & rel_month >= -24 & rel_month <= 24]

est <- feols(AR ~ sunab(first_pub, rel_month) | permno + date,
             data = event_data, cluster = ~permno)

etable(est, se = "cluster")

# Plot leads/lags
iplot(est)

# --------------------------------------------------
# 6. Robustness: Exclude same-industry peers
# --------------------------------------------------
event_data2 <- event_data[, has_peer_treat := any(treat==1), by = .(ind, date)]
est2 <- feols(AR ~ sunab(first_pub, rel_month) | permno + date,
              data = event_data2[has_peer_treat==0], cluster = ~permno)
etable(est2, se="cluster")
```

----------------------------------------------------
6. Expected Results
----------------------------------------------------
Theory suggests markets undervalue hard-to-measure intangibles; hence inclusion should predict positive abnormal returns.

Prior:  
•  Annualised abnormal return ≈ 3 % – 4 % (equal-weight); value-weight somewhat lower (~2 %).  
•  Effect should appear within first 12 months post-publication and taper after 24 months as information diffuses.

----------------------------------------------------
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (1 = strong, 0 = weak)
1. Credible counterfactual (matched DiD) ............... 0.8  
2. Parallel-trend evidence (lead coefficients ≈ 0) ..... 0.8  
3. No manipulation of treatment timing ................. 0.7  
4. No spillovers / interference ........................ 0.6  
5. Robust standard errors & multiple checks ............ 0.9  

Overall: Promising, but residual selection on unobservables and potential spillovers warrant caution.
